theory.title: Make, let y allow con objeto + infinitivo
theory.explanation: Usa make + persona + infinitivo sin to cuando alguien obliga o provoca una acción; let + persona + infinitivo sin to para dar permiso; y allow + persona + to + infinitivo. En pasiva, make va seguido de to + infinitivo: We were made to wait (nos hicieron esperar).
theory.tip: Make / let + persona + infinitivo sin to. Allow + persona + to + infinitivo.

content.passage: The media club has introduced new rules for its members. The teacher lets students borrow cameras, but the school doesn't allow them to film in private areas. During the last project, the director made the team repeat one scene because the sound was unclear. The editor also made everyone check the subtitles. The club allows members to publish their work on the school website after a teacher has approved it.

items.prompt: Describe a rule that lets students use technology.
items.modelAnswer: Our school lets students use tablets during research activities, but they must follow the teacher's instructions. The devices help us find information quickly, although we still need to check whether websites are reliable.

items.prompt: Talk about something your parents let you do as a child.
items.modelAnswer: When I was a child, my parents let me ride my bicycle to the park once I was old enough to understand the road rules. They made me wear a helmet and tell them when I would be home.

items.prompt: Explain what a teacher might make students do for a project.
items.modelAnswer: For a group project, a teacher might make students interview local residents and prepare a short presentation. This helps everyone practise research and communication. The teacher should also allow students to choose their own roles.

items.prompt: What should websites allow users to do?
items.modelAnswer: Websites should allow users to change their privacy settings, correct personal information and delete their accounts. They should also make it easy to report harmful content. People need to understand how their data is used.

items.prompt: Describe a situation where you were made to wait.
items.modelAnswer: I was made to wait at the station for nearly an hour because the train had a technical problem. The staff explained the delay and offered another route. It was frustrating, but I understood that safety came first.

items.prompt: Talk about rules that don't allow certain behaviour.
items.modelAnswer: School rules don't allow students to copy other people's work or use phones during exams. These rules are fair because everyone should have the same opportunity to show what they know.

items.prompt: Explain how a director makes actors prepare.
items.modelAnswer: A director makes actors prepare by giving them the script, explaining the characters and arranging rehearsals. Actors may also be made to repeat a scene until the timing is right.

items.prompt: What do schools allow students to borrow?
items.modelAnswer: Our school allows students to borrow laptops, dictionaries and sports equipment. They have to return everything on time and report any damage. It is useful for students who cannot buy their own equipment.

items.prompt: Give an example of someone making you change your mind.
items.modelAnswer: My friend made me change my mind about buying a new phone. He showed me how to replace the battery in my old one, and it worked perfectly. I realised I didn't need to spend money on a new device.

items.prompt: Compare make, let and allow in three examples.
items.modelAnswer: My parents made me tidy my room, but they let me choose when to do it. The library allows students to borrow several books at once. These examples show that make is stronger, while let and allow give permission.
